mhra-approves-icotrokinra-plaque-psorias.name: MHRA approves icotrokinra for psoriasis
mhra-approves-icotrokinra-plaque-psorias.summary: The MHRA has approved icotrokinra (Icotyde), a once-daily tablet, for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in people aged 12 and over.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in October 2026.
The approval covers adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg.
It applies to people who are candidates for systemic therapy.
The MHRA says four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants showed benefit over placebo at week 16.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has approved icotrokinra hydrochloride (Icotyde) for the treatment of moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 years and older who weigh at least 40 kg. The medicine is a tablet taken once a day, and the marketing authorisation was granted to Janssen-Cilag Limited.

The approval applies to people who are candidates for systemic therapy, which means treatment that acts throughout the body rather than on the skin alone.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA says its decision rested on four phase 3 trials with about 2,500 participants, 72 of them adolescents aged 12 to under 18 who weighed at least 40 kg. In all four trials, icotrokinra showed benefit over placebo at week 16. The site's psoriasis page explains the condition.

source.title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis

references.title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis

mhra-authorises-onswik-weekly-insulin.name: MHRA authorises weekly insulin Onswik
mhra-authorises-onswik-weekly-insulin.summary: The MHRA has authorised Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa), a once-weekly insulin injection, for adults with type 2 diabetes.
keyPoints: The MHRA authorised Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) for adults with type 2 diabetes on 13 October 2026.
It is a once-weekly injection.
The MHRA says it may reduce the number of injections needed from up to 365 a year to 52.
The MHRA names low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) as the most common adverse reaction.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has authorised Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) for adults with type 2 diabetes. Onswik is a once-weekly injection, and the MHRA says this treatment option may reduce the number of injections needed from up to 365 a year to 52.

The licence was granted to Eli Lilly Nederland B.V. through the ACCESS procedure. The summary of product characteristics and the patient leaflet are to be published later on the MHRA Products website.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: An MHRA executive director said that in trials, weekly dosing gave blood sugar control similar to once-daily basal insulin. The MHRA reports that hypoglycaemia, or low blood sugar, was the most common adverse reaction. The site's type 2 diabetes and insulin pages give background.

source.title: MHRA authorises Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) for adults with type 2 diabetes

references.title: MHRA authorises Onswik (insulin efsitora alfa) for adults with type 2 diabetes

mhra-osimertinib-muscle-toxicity-reminde.name: MHRA: osimertinib and muscle toxicity
mhra-osimertinib-muscle-toxicity-reminde.summary: The MHRA's October 2026 Safety Roundup covers osimertinib (Tagrisso) and muscle toxicity, including a rare breakdown of muscle tissue called rhabdomyolysis.
keyPoints: The MHRA's October 2026 Safety Roundup, issued on 27 October 2026, includes an item on osimertinib (Tagrisso) and skeletal muscle toxicity.
The MHRA says myositis and raised blood creatine phosphokinase (CPK) are recognised side effects of osimertinib.
Cases of rhabdomyolysis have been reported after marketing in other countries, and the MHRA had received no UK Yellow Card reports to date.
The MHRA says patients should be told before treatment to report unexplained muscle symptoms and dark urine.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says myositis, which is muscle inflammation, and a raised blood level of creatine phosphokinase (CPK) are recognised side effects of osimertinib (Tagrisso). It adds that cases of rhabdomyolysis have been reported after marketing in other countries, but that it has not received any UK Yellow Card reports to date. Rhabdomyolysis is the breakdown of muscle tissue.

The roundup says that, before treatment starts, patients should be advised to report any unexplained muscle pain, tenderness, weakness, trouble moving arms or legs, dark tea-coloured urine or decreased urination.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA says a suspected rise in CPK, myositis or rhabdomyolysis calls for clinical evaluation and treatment. In severe events, osimertinib treatment may need to be interrupted, and the MHRA points clinicians to the product's summary of product characteristics. The site's lung cancer page explains the condition osimertinib is used for.

mhra-fluenz-nasal-flu-vaccine-fainting.name: MHRA updates Fluenz fainting information
mhra-fluenz-nasal-flu-vaccine-fainting.summary: The MHRA's September 2026 Safety Roundup says Fluenz nasal flu vaccine information now notes a higher chance of fainting soon after the spray is given.
keyPoints: The MHRA's September 2026 Safety Roundup says the Fluenz product information has been updated to reflect an increased risk of syncope (fainting).
The risk applies right after the nasal spray is given.
The MHRA says vaccine providers should have procedures in place to prevent injury from fainting and to manage fainting reactions.
The MHRA says the information is not in the patient leaflet for this season's campaign.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA's Safety Roundup for September 2026, published on 29 September 2026, says the product information for the Fluenz nasal spray flu vaccine now notes a higher risk of fainting right after the spray is given. The MHRA says procedures should be in place to prevent injury from fainting and to manage fainting reactions.

The MHRA also says this information is not included in the patient information leaflet for this season's campaign, so clinicians should tell parents and patients about the risk beforehand.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA's notice is addressed to healthcare professionals who give the vaccine. The site's influenza page and its pages on the flu vaccine give background on the vaccine.

mhra-authorises-orforglipron-foundayo.name: MHRA authorises orforglipron (Foundayo)
mhra-authorises-orforglipron-foundayo.summary: The MHRA authorised orforglipron (Foundayo), a GLP-1 tablet, for weight management and type 2 diabetes, saying the UK is the first country in Europe to do so.
keyPoints: The MHRA authorised orforglipron (Foundayo) on 10 August 2026.
The MHRA says the UK is the first country in Europe to authorise this GLP-1 tablet for weight management and type 2 diabetes.
For weight management it is licensed for adults who meet set body mass index and weight-related health criteria, alongside a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity.
For diabetes it is licensed to improve blood sugar control in adults whose type 2 diabetes is not controlled well enough.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it authorised orforglipron, sold as Foundayo, on 10 August 2026. It describes orforglipron as a GLP-1 receptor agonist taken as a tablet, and says the UK is the first country in Europe to authorise it for weight management and type 2 diabetes.

For weight management, the licence covers adults who meet set criteria for body mass index and weight-related health conditions, and treatment is used together with a reduced-calorie diet and more physical activity. For type 2 diabetes, it is licensed to improve glycaemic (blood sugar) control in people whose diabetes is insufficiently controlled.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The announcement concerns the MHRA's licensing decision. The site's pages on type 2 diabetes, weight and GLP-1 receptor agonists give background.

source.title: UK first in Europe to authorise orforglipron for weight management and type 2 diabetes

references.title: UK first in Europe to authorise orforglipron for weight management and type 2 diabetes

mhra-approves-remibrutinib-chronic-urtic.name: MHRA approves remibrutinib for urticaria
mhra-approves-remibrutinib-chronic-urtic.summary: The MHRA has approved remibrutinib (Rhapsido) tablets for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria whose symptoms antihistamines do not control well enough.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved remibrutinib (Rhapsido) for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU).
It is for people whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by antihistamines.
The approval used the International Recognition Procedure, Route B.
The MHRA cites two main clinical studies with 925 adults, in which remibrutinib reduced itch and hive symptoms more than placebo.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says it has approved remibrutinib (Rhapsido) tablets for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria (CSU) whose symptoms are not adequately controlled by antihistamines. The approval came through the International Recognition Procedure (IRP), Route B.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA says the decision rests on two main clinical studies involving 925 adults who had not responded well enough to H1 antihistamines. In these studies, people treated with remibrutinib had significantly greater reductions in itch and hive symptoms than people given placebo.

The MHRA says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of remibrutinib under close review. The site's hives page explains the condition.

source.title: MHRA approves remibrutinib for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria

references.title: MHRA approves remibrutinib for adults with chronic spontaneous urticaria

mhra-approves-semaglutide-wegovy-mash.name: MHRA approves Wegovy for liver disease
mhra-approves-semaglutide-wegovy-mash.summary: The MHRA approved Wegovy (semaglutide) on 3 July 2026 for MASH, a form of liver disease, in adults with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved Wegovy (semaglutide) on 3 July 2026 for MASH in adults with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis.
The approval is conditional on further results from an ongoing study being submitted.
The announcement says people with MASH cannot yet get semaglutide for this condition on the NHS.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has approved Wegovy (semaglutide) for MASH in adults with moderate-to-advanced liver fibrosis. MASH stands for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, a form of liver disease linked to fat build-up and inflammation in the liver.

The approval is conditional: the company must submit further results from an ongoing study in adults with MASH and moderate to advanced liver scarring.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The announcement states that people with MASH cannot yet get semaglutide for this condition on the NHS. The site's pages on fatty liver disease and semaglutide give background.

source.title: Semaglutide (Wegovy) approved to treat form of liver disease

references.title: Semaglutide (Wegovy) approved to treat form of liver disease

mhra-authorises-inqlexzo-bladder-cancer.name: MHRA authorises Inqlexzo for bladder cancer
mhra-authorises-inqlexzo-bladder-cancer.summary: The MHRA authorised Inqlexzo, a gemcitabine system placed in the bladder, for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
keyPoints: The MHRA authorised the gemcitabine delivery system Inqlexzo for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.
It is for adults who cannot have, or choose not to have, surgery to remove the bladder.
A healthcare professional places the system in the bladder using a catheter, and it releases gemcitabine locally.
The MHRA says it will keep monitoring the safety and effectiveness of the system.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has authorised an intravesical gemcitabine delivery system, Inqlexzo, for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer. The authorisation covers adults who are ineligible for, or have chosen not to have, radical cystectomy, which is surgery to remove the bladder.

A healthcare professional places the device in the bladder using a catheter, and it releases the chemotherapy medicine gemcitabine inside the bladder.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA says the authorisation is supported by results from a clinical study in adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk disease and carcinoma in situ. The MHRA says it will keep monitoring the safety and effectiveness of the system. The site's bladder cancer page explains the condition.

source.title: MHRA authorises gemcitabine delivery system for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer

references.title: MHRA authorises gemcitabine delivery system for adults with BCG-unresponsive high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer

mhra-approves-lower-carbon-clenil-inhale.name: MHRA approves lower-carbon asthma inhalers
mhra-approves-lower-carbon-clenil-inhale.summary: The MHRA approved new versions of two Clenil Modulite beclometasone inhalers for asthma that use a next-generation propellant with a lower carbon impact.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved new versions of two Clenil Modulite beclometasone inhalers on 21 July 2026.
They are for maintenance treatment of asthma in adults and children.
They use a next-generation propellant designed to reduce environmental impact.
The new versions are due to reach UK patients later in 2026.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says it has approved new versions of two Clenil Modulite beclometasone inhalers for the maintenance treatment of asthma in adults and children. The new inhalers use a next-generation propellant, and the company says this is the first inhaler authorised with that propellant.

The MHRA describes the active ingredient as a corticosteroid that reduces inflammation in the airways. It says the inhalers keep the same established treatment while reducing environmental impact.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA lists oral thrush, hoarseness and throat irritation as the most common side effects. It says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of beclometasone dipropionate under close review. The new versions are expected to reach UK patients later in 2026. The site's asthma and beclometasone pages give background.

source.title: MHRA approves world's first lower-carbon beclometasone inhalers for patients with asthma

references.title: MHRA approves world's first lower-carbon beclometasone inhalers for patients with asthma

mhra-approves-zynyz-merkel-cell-cancer.name: MHRA approves Zynyz for Merkel cell cancer
mhra-approves-zynyz-merkel-cell-cancer.summary: The MHRA approved retifanlimab (Zynyz) on 6 July 2026 as the first treatment for adults with advanced Merkel cell skin cancer.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved retifanlimab (Zynyz) on 6 July 2026.
It is the first treatment for adults with advanced Merkel cell skin cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be cured by surgery or radiotherapy.
The MHRA describes it as an immunotherapy given by infusion.
In a study of 101 adults, 53.5% responded to retifanlimab.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says it approved retifanlimab (Zynyz) on 6 July 2026 as the first treatment for adults with advanced Merkel cell skin cancer. The approval is for cancer that has spread or returned and cannot be cured with surgery or radiotherapy, and it came through the International Recognition Procedure.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA explains that retifanlimab is an immunotherapy that helps the body's immune system recognise and attack cancer cells. It is given as a diluted intravenous infusion over 30 minutes.

The MHRA reports that in a study of 101 adults who had not previously been treated for advanced disease, 53.5% responded to retifanlimab. The site's skin cancer page explains the condition.

source.title: MHRA approves Retifanlimab (ZYNYZ) for the treatment of advanced Merkel cell skin cancer

references.title: MHRA approves Retifanlimab (ZYNYZ) for the treatment of advanced Merkel cell skin cancer

mhra-bladder-anticholinergics-dementia-r.name: MHRA review of bladder drugs and dementia
mhra-bladder-anticholinergics-dementia-r.summary: The MHRA's review found the evidence insufficient to confirm that bladder anticholinergic medicines directly raise dementia risk, but a small increased risk cannot be ruled out.
keyPoints: The MHRA published a review of bladder anticholinergic medicines and the risk of dementia on 27 July 2026.
It found the evidence insufficient to confirm a direct causal link.
It says a small increased risk cannot be ruled out completely because of limitations in the studies.
The MHRA advises clinicians to limit the number of anticholinergic medicines older people take and to use the lowest dose.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA has published a public assessment report on the risk of dementia with bladder anticholinergic medicines. The Commission on Human Medicines had recommended a review of the evidence on a possible link.

The MHRA concluded that the evidence is insufficient to confirm that these medicines directly cause dementia. It says a small increased risk cannot be ruled out completely because of limitations in the studies.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The MHRA's advice for clinicians is to limit the number of anticholinergic medicines that older people take and to use the lowest dose. Questions about an individual's treatment are for the prescriber or pharmacist. The site's pages on urinary incontinence and Alzheimer's disease give background.

source.title: Bladder Anticholinergics: review of risk of dementia

references.title: Bladder Anticholinergics: review of risk of dementia

mhra-domperidone-phaeochromocytoma-contr.name: MHRA: domperidone and phaeochromocytoma
mhra-domperidone-phaeochromocytoma-contr.summary: The MHRA says domperidone is now contraindicated in confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma because of a risk of severe hypertension.
keyPoints: The MHRA published a Drug Safety Update on 21 July 2026 about domperidone.
Domperidone is now contraindicated in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma.
The reason is a risk of severe hypertension (very high blood pressure).
The MHRA had received no UK Yellow Card reports of this event.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA says a recent European review of safety data identified an association between domperidone and episodes of severe hypertension in patients with phaeochromocytoma, after a small number of reports. Phaeochromocytoma is a rare tumour of the adrenal gland.

As a result, domperidone is now contraindicated in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma, which means it should not be used in them.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA tells prescribers that patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma who are taking domperidone should have treatment stopped and be switched to an alternative. It adds that domperidone can unmask the tumour, so a severe hypertensive episode in someone taking it should prompt consideration of further investigation.

The MHRA says it has not received any UK Yellow Card reports of severe hypertension with domperidone in patients with phaeochromocytoma, and asks that suspected side effects be reported through the Yellow Card scheme. Anyone with questions about their own treatment can ask the prescriber or pharmacist.

source.title: Domperidone: new contraindication in patients with phaeochromocytoma due to the risk of severe hypertension

references.title: Domperidone: new contraindication in patients with phaeochromocytoma due to the risk of severe hypertension

mhra-seizes-counterfeit-weight-loss-pens.name: MHRA seizes £2m of fake weight loss pens
mhra-seizes-counterfeit-weight-loss-pens.summary: The MHRA and West Midlands Police seized counterfeit weight loss pens worth about £2 million in Birmingham, including fake retatrutide and tirzepatide products.
keyPoints: The MHRA and West Midlands Police seized counterfeit weight loss medicines worth about £2 million in a raid on an industrial unit in Birmingham in October 2026.
The haul included more than 12,000 counterfeit retatrutide and tirzepatide pens.
The MHRA says the products were never checked for safety, quality or effectiveness.
The MHRA says retatrutide is not authorised for use in the UK.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says it worked with West Midlands Police to seize counterfeit weight loss medicines worth about £2 million from an industrial unit in Birmingham. Officers took more than 12,000 counterfeit retatrutide and tirzepatide pens, plus packaging for around 30,000 more products.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA says the products were never checked for safety, quality or effectiveness, so their contents and any contamination are unknown. It also says retatrutide is not authorised for use in the UK and that selling it outside legitimate clinical trials is illegal and a public health risk.

The site's pages on tirzepatide and weight give background on the genuine medicine and the topic.

source.title: Counterfeit weight loss pens worth £2 million seized by MHRA and West Midlands Police

references.title: Counterfeit weight loss pens worth £2 million seized by MHRA and West Midlands Police

mhra-recall-zentiva-fingolimod-capsules.name: MHRA recalls one batch of fingolimod
mhra-recall-zentiva-fingolimod-capsules.summary: The MHRA issued a Class 2 recall of one batch of Fingolimod Zentiva capsules on 20 August 2026 as a precaution over possible metal particle contamination.
keyPoints: The MHRA issued a Class 2 medicines recall on 20 August 2026 for one batch of Fingolimod Zentiva capsules.
Zentiva Pharma UK Limited issued the recall as a precaution because of a potential risk of contamination with metal particles.
The particles were found during shelf-life testing, and no reports had been received.
For patients, the notice advises contacting their pharmacy and not stopping medication without speaking to a clinician.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says Zentiva Pharma UK Limited is recalling one batch of Fingolimod Zentiva capsules, batch number 4L01372H, as a precaution. The reason is a potential risk of contamination with metal particles, which were found during shelf-life testing. The MHRA says no reports have been received to date.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The notice tells dispensers to stop supplying the affected batch and to quarantine remaining stock for return through their supplier's approved process. For patients, the advice is to contact their pharmacy first and not to stop their medication without speaking to a clinician.

The recall was classed as Class 2 and listed in the MHRA's August 2026 Safety Roundup. The site's multiple sclerosis page gives background on the condition.

source.title: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Zentiva Pharma UK Limited, Fingolimod Zentiva 0.5 mg Capsules, EL(26)A/37

references.title: Class 2 Medicines Recall: Zentiva Pharma UK Limited, Fingolimod Zentiva 0.5 mg Capsules, EL(26)A/37

mhra-ketone-test-strips-supply-disruptio.name: MHRA alert on ketone test strip supply
mhra-ketone-test-strips-supply-disruptio.summary: The MHRA warned of disruption to blood ketone testing after Nova Biomedical recalled StatStrip ketone test strip lots and paused distribution.
keyPoints: The MHRA issued a Device Safety Information notice on 9 October 2026 about Nova Biomedical StatStrip ketone test strips.
Nova Biomedical has recalled specified lots after repeated quality-control failures and paused distribution of those lots.
The company says it cannot replenish UK stock for roughly four weeks.
The MHRA says losing timely ketone testing could delay recognition and treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says Nova Biomedical has recalled specified lots of StatStrip ketone test strips after repeated quality-control failures and has paused distribution of those lots. Any further lots that fail quality control are to be withdrawn, which could steadily reduce the strips available for clinical use. The company has said it cannot replenish UK stock for about four weeks.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA warns that losing timely ketone testing can delay recognition, escalation and treatment of diabetic ketoacidosis (DKA), and that this could contribute to serious harm or death. DKA is a serious complication of diabetes.

Where supply is limited, the MHRA advises clinicians to prioritise testing for patients at greatest risk, including those with suspected or established DKA, children, and acutely unwell people with type 1 diabetes. A separate National Patient Safety Alert on the supply disruption was issued on 13 October 2026. The site's type 1 diabetes page gives background on the condition.

source.title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip ketone test strips: risk of disruption to blood ketone testing due to quality-control failures and supply interruption DSI/2026/013

references.title: Nova Biomedical StatStrip ketone test strips: risk of disruption to blood ketone testing due to quality-control failures and supply interruption DSI/2026/013

mhra-casgevy-children-aged-five-and-over.name: MHRA extends Casgevy to ages five and over
mhra-casgevy-children-aged-five-and-over.summary: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of Casgevy to children aged five and over with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
keyPoints: The MHRA extended the UK authorisation of the gene-editing treatment Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) to children aged five and over.
It is for severe sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia.
Casgevy was previously authorised in the UK for people aged 12 and over.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body: The MHRA says Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel) can now be used in eligible children from the age of five with severe sickle cell disease or transfusion-dependent beta thalassaemia. Before this decision, the UK authorisation covered people aged 12 and over.

body.heading: What it means
body.body:
The MHRA describes both conditions as serious, lifelong conditions that can in some cases be fatal. It explains that Casgevy works by editing the faulty gene in a patient's bone marrow stem cells so that the body produces functioning haemoglobin.

The MHRA decision is separate from NHS access, which in England is decided through NICE. The site's anaemia page gives background on blood disorders.

source.title: MHRA approves gene-editing treatment for children aged five and over with serious inherited blood disorders

references.title: MHRA approves gene-editing treatment for children aged five and over with serious inherited blood disorders

mhra-nice-aficamten-hypertrophic-cardiom.name: MHRA and NICE decisions on aficamten
mhra-nice-aficamten-hypertrophic-cardiom.summary: The MHRA approved aficamten (Myqorzo) for obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy on the same day NICE recommended it, in a co-ordinated decision.
keyPoints: The MHRA approved aficamten (Myqorzo) for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, and NICE recommended it at the same time.
The GOV.UK release says around 6,600 people in England will be able to access the treatment.
NICE published its final guidance two weeks faster than its standard process.
The MHRA says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of aficamten under close review.

body.heading: What was announced
body.body:
The MHRA and NICE made co-ordinated decisions on aficamten (Myqorzo), a once-daily pill for symptomatic obstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy. The GOV.UK release says the treatment was recommended by NICE at the same time as it was approved by the MHRA.

It says around 6,600 people in England with this serious heart condition will be able to access the treatment, and that NICE published its final guidance two weeks faster than its standard processes.

body.heading: What it means
body.body: The release credits closer working between the two bodies, under which licensing and NHS value assessment run together. The MHRA says it will keep the safety and effectiveness of aficamten under close review. The site's heart failure page gives background on heart conditions.

source.title: Thousands of patients to benefit from new daily pill for serious heart condition following co-ordinated MHRA and NICE decisions

references.title: Thousands of patients to benefit from new daily pill for serious heart condition following co-ordinated MHRA and NICE decisions
